HUNTINGTON, W.Va., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Energy Services of America Corporation (the "Company" or "Energy Services") (Nasdaq: ESOA) today announced that its subsidiary, FAMCO Acquisition, Inc., has completed the acquisition of substantially all of the operating assets of FAMCO, Inc. ("FAMCO"), a West Virginia utility contractor focused primarily on water and sewer infrastructure.

The acquisition was completed for a base purchase price of $6.95 million, subject to the adjustments and other terms set forth in the Asset Purchase Agreement. The consideration consists of cash and Energy Services common stock, with a portion of the purchase price withheld pending a post-closing true-up.

FAMCO brings an experienced workforce, equipment fleet and customer relationships in water and sewer infrastructure. The acquisition complements Energy Services' existing water and utility construction operations and expands its capabilities in these markets.

"We are excited to add FAMCO to the Energy Services team," said Douglas Reynolds, President of Energy Services. "FAMCO brings experienced people, equipment and customer relationships that complement our existing operations and further strengthen our capabilities in water and utility construction."

About Energy Services

Energy Services of America Corporation (NASDAQ: ESOA), headquartered in Huntington, WV, is a contractor and service company that operates primarily in the mid-Atlantic and Central regions of the United States and provides services to customers in the natural gas, petroleum, water distribution, automotive, chemical, and power industries. Energy Services employs 1,400+ employees on a regular basis. The Company's core values are safety, quality, and production.

RESTON, Va., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- General Dynamics (NYSE:GD) announced today that Amy Johnson has been appointed as president of GDIT, effective November 3.

Johnson is a 27-year veteran of General Dynamics Mission Systems, where she held increasingly senior roles in engineering, engineering management and business leadership across cybersecurity, defense electronics, space and intelligence systems, most recently as vice president and general manager for Space, Cyber and Intelligence. She earned bachelor's and master's degrees in computer science and computer systems engineering. 

"Amy has a proven track record of leading teams to solve complex and highly technical challenges for our customers," said Phebe Novakovic, CEO of General Dynamics. "I am confident that her dynamic leadership, operational rigor and deep commitment to our values and culture will deliver value to our customers, employees and shareholders."

GDIT delivers digital modernization, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and software development solutions to the U.S. federal government, defense, intelligence agencies and other customers. SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Nektar Therapeutics (NASDAQ: NKTR) today announced that, on October 20, 2026, the Organization and Compensation Committee of Nektar's Board of Directors granted non-qualified stock options to purchase an aggregate of 45,750 shares of its common stock and 2,775 restricted stock units (RSUs) to sixteen newly-hired employees under Nektar's 2025 Inducement Plan, as amended.

Nektar's 2025 Inducement Plan was adopted by its Board of Directors on November 6, 2025 and amended on September 23, 2026 to increase the number of shares of common stock reserved and available for issuance under the plan by 250,000 shares, for a total of 500,000 shares. The plan is used exclusively for the grant of equity awards to individuals who were not previously an employee or non-employee director of Nektar (or following a bona fide period of non‑employment), as an inducement material to such individual's entering into employment with Nektar, pursuant to Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4).

The stock options have an exercise price per share equal to $39.22, which is equal to the closing price of Nektar's common stock on October 20, 2026. The stock options have an eight-year term and will vest over four years with 1/4th of the shares vesting on the one-year anniversary of the employee's grant date and 1/48th of the shares vesting monthly thereafter over the next three years, subject to each employee's continued employment with Nektar on such vesting dates. The RSUs vest over four years with 1/4th of the shares vesting following the one-year anniversary of the employee's grant date and 1/16th of the shares vesting quarterly thereafter over the next three years, subject to each employee's continued employment with Nektar on the applicable vesting dates. Nektar Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing treatments that address the underlying immunological dysfunction in autoimmune and chronic inflammatory diseases. Nektar's lead product candidate, rezpegaldesleukin (REZPEG, or NKTR-358), is a novel, first-in-class regulatory T cell stimulator being evaluated in atopic dermatitis, alopecia areata, and Type 1 diabetes mellitus. Nektar's pipeline also includes preclinical bivalent tumor necrosis factor receptor type II (TNFR2) antibody and bispecific programs, NKTR-0165 and NKTR-0166, and a modified hematopoietic colony stimulating factor (CSF) protein, NKTR-422.

The filing underscores the Monterey Peninsula's continued need for drought-proof water supplies and describes strategies to be implemented to offset project cost

PACIFIC GROVE, Calif., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Today, California American Water submitted an application to the California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) updating the project cost estimates, a low-cost financing framework, and a proposal for rate treatment for the Monterey Peninsula Water Supply Project's desalination facilities.

California American Water has been working with state regulatory agencies for decades to address the Monterey Peninsula's water supply crisis and lift the State Water Board's cease-and-desist order, which has limited the region's economic growth and prevented sustainable housing development. This work has reduced pumping from the Carmel River by 75 percent, to date.

In 2018, the CPUC authorized the desalination project as the best solution to address Monterey's long-term water supply needs, aligning with California's Water Resiliency Portfolio, which calls for the implementation of desalination. The CPUC approved environmental planning documents and verified supply and demand estimates that confirmed the region faces a water deficit by 2050. Subsequent to the 2018 CPUC authorization, lengthy approval and permitting processes, as well as continuous legal challenges, have extended the project timeline. These delays have exposed the project to labor and construction material cost escalations, as well as significant engineering, procurement and legal expense, resulting in a total construction estimate of $825 million.

"California American Water remains committed to ensuring the Monterey Peninsula has a reliable water supply into the future, and we are taking steps to pursue alternative sources of financing to minimize the costs and protect affordability for our customers," said California American Water President Sarah Leeper. "To mitigate the impacts of the project costs, our application proposes financing and ratemaking measures estimated to reduce the impact on customers by $588 million over the 40-year life of the project."

The California American Water team is proposing project financing and rate structures to lower the overall cost to protect Monterey's customers and protect the future of water supply on the peninsula. The company will continue working with the CPUC and state and local leaders to discuss other potential cost reductions in order to deliver a drought-proof water supply project.

California American Water and its coalition of partners, including leaders in labor, business, community and environmental advocacy, continue to view desalination as the best technical solution to diversify and drought-proof Monterey's water supplies. The CPUC filing provides new cost data, financing opportunities, and ratemaking considerations for regulators and stakeholders to evaluate and provides that the project proceeds based on sound data, appropriate funding, and clear measures to promote affordability and mitigate rate impacts.

For further updates on California American Water's work in Monterey, visit the project website www.watersupplyproject.org.

American Water (NYSE: AWK) is the largest regulated water and wastewater utility company in the United States. With a history dating back to 1886 and celebrating 140 years in 2026, We Keep Life Flowing® by providing safe, clean, reliable and affordable drinking water and wastewater services to approximately 14 million people with regulated operations in 14 states and on 19 military installations. PHILADELPHIA, Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Board of Trustees of Aberdeen Multi-Market Income Fund (NYSE: MMT) has approved a 1-for-4 reverse stock split of the Fund's issued and outstanding common shares, effective prior to the opening of trading on November 9, 2026.

The Board approved the reverse stock split to increase the Fund's per-share market price. The Board believes a higher share price may reduce certain trading and administrative frictions associated with lower-priced securities, increase the Fund's suitability for certain investment platforms and intermediary programs, and better align the Fund's share price with industry trading conventions.

The aggregate value of a shareholder's investment is not expected to change solely as a result of the reverse stock split, although the market value of Fund shares will continue to fluctuate based on market conditions.

Under the terms of the transaction, every four common shares will be consolidated into one common share. No fractional shares will be issued; fractional share entitlements will be aggregated and sold, with the net proceeds distributed to affected shareholders. The transaction will apply equally to all shareholders and will not affect any shareholder's proportionate ownership interest, other than minor adjustments resulting from the treatment of fractional shares.

Following the transaction, the Fund's common shares will continue to trade on the New York Stock Exchange under the symbol MMT. A new CUSIP number will be assigned to the Fund.

Initiative enables suppliers through renewable energy aggregation and supplier capability building

LAUSANNE, Switzerland & SAN JOSE, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Logitech International (SIX: LOGN) (Nasdaq: LOGI) today announced the launch of Chain Reaction, a global supply chain decarbonization program designed to help supply partners cut carbon emissions, optimize factory operations and unlock shared business growth. The initiative marks an expansion of Logitech’s climate strategy, providing direct operational support to help suppliers build their own decarbonization roadmaps while advancing Logitech’s science-based target to halve its Scope 3 greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 2030.

Core Pillars of Chain Reaction

Launching with an initial cohort of 17 key suppliers, Chain Reaction delivers collaborative enablement across four pillars:

  • Affordable clean energy: Convenes suppliers to aggregate purchasing power and collectively procure high-standard renewable energy instruments. This secures clean electricity at competitive pricing, mitigating long-term volatility and energy risk.
  • Energy and greenhouse gas evaluations: Supports supplier-led factory evaluations to identify energy, thermal and mechanical efficiencies. This empowers suppliers to define reduction targets and roadmaps that serve their entire customer base.
  • Expert support and guidance: Provides technical workshops, roundtables and innovation sessions, alongside co-developed reporting tools. These are designed to streamline carbon accounting and eliminate administrative overhead.
  • Commercial recognition: Integrates carbon transparency and decarbonization into regular business reviews and new business awards, ensuring manufacturing partners gain executive visibility and recognition for measurable carbon reductions.

In fiscal year 2026, Logitech already achieved a 33% reduction in its total Scope 3 carbon footprint compared to its 2021 baseline1. Chain Reaction builds on this momentum by empowering suppliers to identify carbon hotspots and execute practical engineering solutions directly within their facilities and supply chains.

“Real value-chain decarbonization happens directly on the factory floor,” said Elaine Laird, chief people and sustainability officer at Logitech. “Our suppliers understand their operations best. Chain Reaction helps our manufacturing partners access the practical tools, technical evaluations and clean energy solutions they need to optimize their operations and lead their own decarbonization roadmaps.”

To support participating facilities, the program provides technical workshops on establishing GHG baselines, direct access to subject matter experts and pathways to pilot cutting-edge innovations through the Logitech Future Positive Challenge.

“By integrating carbon transparency and decarbonization progress into our commercial metrics, we are enabling more value for our suppliers to grow with Logitech,” said Sree Chenincherry, chief supply chain operations officer at Logitech. “From an operational standpoint, decarbonization and efficiency go hand-in-hand. Equipping our manufacturing partners to reduce energy waste and transition to clean power unlocks structural cost savings, mitigates long-term volatility and strengthens our entire shared value chain.”

About Logitech

Logitech creates design-led, software-enabled hardware solutions that help businesses thrive and bring people together when working, creating and gaming in the age of AI. As the point of connection between people and the digital world, our mission is to extend human potential in work and play, in a way that is good for people and the planet. Founded in 1981, Logitech International is a Swiss public company listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange (LOGN) and on the Nasdaq Global Select Market (LOGI). All other trademarks are the property of their respective owners. For more information about Logitech and its products, visit the company’s website at www.logitech.com.

Key Terms

scope 3technical
Scope 3 describes all greenhouse gas emissions that occur upstream and downstream of a company’s direct operations—things like emissions from suppliers, transportation, product use, and disposal. Think of it as the hidden carbon footprint tied to everything a business buys, sells, or enables; it matters to investors because these indirect emissions can drive regulatory costs, supply-chain disruption, consumer preference shifts, and long-term valuation risk that aren’t visible on a company’s factory floor or utility bill.

Key Terms

financial assets at fair value through profit or lossfinancial
An accounting category for investments and contracts that are updated to their current market price on the balance sheet, with any gain or loss immediately shown in the company’s profit or loss statement. Investors care because this treatment makes reported earnings swing with market prices, so short-term market moves can boost or cut reported profits quickly — like revaluing a garage full of cars at today’s resale prices and recording the change as income or loss.
earnings per sharefinancial
Earnings per share represent the amount of profit a company makes for each share of its stock, similar to how a pie’s total size can be divided into slices for each person. It helps investors understand how profitable the company is on a per-share basis, making it easier to compare its performance over time or against other companies. Higher earnings per share generally indicate better profitability and can influence a company's stock value.
View in glossary
non-controlling interestsfinancial
An ownership stake in a subsidiary held by outside shareholders rather than the parent company, representing the portion of that subsidiary’s assets and profits the parent does not control. For investors, it shows what part of consolidated earnings and equity belongs to others — like a roommate who owns part of a house — which affects how much value and profit per share are truly attributable to the parent company’s shareholders.
property, plant and equipmentfinancial
Property, plant and equipment are a company’s long-term physical assets—land, buildings, factories, machinery, vehicles and similar items—used in day-to-day operations rather than held for sale. They appear on the balance sheet at cost less accumulated depreciation (except land) and represent the resources a business uses to produce goods or services; changes in these assets affect future production capacity, cash spending for maintenance or replacement, and reported profits through depreciation.

Ifetroban was well tolerated in patients with systemic sclerosis

NASHVILLE, Tenn., Oct. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Cumberland Pharmaceuticals Inc. (NASDAQ: CPIX), an innovation-driven biopharmaceutical company advancing new therapies that address significant unmet medical needs, announces top-line results from its Phase 2a ASSIST-SSc trial evaluating oral ifetroban for patients with systemic sclerosis ("SSc"). These results support the safety and tolerability of ifetroban in this rare disease population. Cumberland will next complete correlative biomarker studies using specimens collected during the trial, along with an evaluation of cardiac imaging from patients continuing on the open-label extension.

SSc is a rare autoimmune disease characterized by excess collagen deposition resulting in skin thickening, cardiovascular disease, gastrointestinal problems, and more, and affects approximately 100,000 individuals in the U.S. Current therapies target specific manifestations of SSc, and approved options are available for SSc-associated interstitial lung disease. However, there is no approved therapy directed at the primary cardiac issues associated with SSc. Both cardiac and pulmonary manifestations remain among the leading causes of mortality for patients with the disease.

Ifetroban is a once-daily oral medication that works by blocking the thromboxane receptor, which plays a key role in inflammation, vascular dysfunction and fibrosis. In preclinical models of pulmonary arterial hypertension and heart disease, ifetroban treatment was associated with a reduction in fibrosis and provided cardioprotective effects (West 2016). A delay or inhibition of tissue fibrosis and improved cardiac function could provide significant improvement in quality of life for SSc patients. These preclinical results were foundational to the development of this Phase 2a clinical trial.

The 12-month Phase 2a ASSIST-SSc trial (NCT02682511) was a pilot trial to evaluate the safety of oral ifetroban in patients with SSc. Patients with either diffuse cutaneous (dcSSc) or pulmonary arterial hypertension (SSc-PAH) manifestations were randomized to receive ifetroban or matching placebo. A total of 31 subjects received ifetroban (22 dcSSc and 9 SSc-PAH) and 10 subjects received placebo (9 dcSSc and 1 SSc-PAH). Safety was evaluated by the frequency of treatment emergent adverse events between treatment groups. Exploratory efficacy endpoints were evaluated by SSc cohort to assess the effect of ifetroban on multiple aspects of SSc disease, including cardiovascular, pulmonary, skin, activity and quality of life.

Ifetroban was generally well tolerated, with a safety profile consistent with prior experience. As in prior ifetroban studies, gastrointestinal adverse events were more frequent in the ifetroban group than in the placebo group; the majority were mild and resolved. A modest increase in bleeding-related adverse events was also observed with ifetroban, in keeping with its mechanism as a thromboxane prostanoid receptor antagonist, and these events were predominantly mild. No serious adverse event during the 12-month treatment period was assessed by the medical monitor as related to study drug.

The majority of subjects in both treatment groups showed limited disease progression during the study, which reduced the ability of a trial of this size to detect a treatment difference. This Phase 2a trial was not designed or powered to evaluate efficacy, and the sample size and exploratory analytic approach preclude efficacy conclusions.

Cumberland has reviewed the results from both the dcSSc and SSc-PAH cohorts with clinical experts in SSc. As next steps, the Company plans to submit the clinical study report to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration ("FDA") and to also complete correlative biomarker studies using specimens collected during the trial, along with an evaluation of cardiac imaging from patients continuing on the open-label extension. Those findings will inform Cumberland's decision on the further development of ifetroban in SSc.

About Systemic Sclerosis (SSc)

SSc is a rare autoimmune connective tissue disease which is characterized by rapidly progressing fibrosis and atrophy in the musculoskeletal system and internal organs including the lungs, heart, gastrointestinal tract and kidneys. While approved therapies exist for certain pulmonary manifestations, no therapy is currently approved to treat or prevent the primary cardiac involvement of SSc.

Cumberland Pharmaceuticals Inc. is an innovation-focused biopharmaceutical company developing new therapies to address significant unmet medical needs and improve the quality of patient care. The Company is advancing a clinical pipeline of late-stage product candidates across multiple therapeutic areas with significant unmet medical needs.

Cumberland's Phase 2 clinical programs are also evaluating ifetroban in patients with Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy, Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis and Cancer Metastasis.

Key Terms

mark-to-marketfinancial
"Mark-to-market" is a method of valuing assets or investments based on their current market price, rather than their original cost or value. It helps investors see the most up-to-date worth of their holdings, much like checking the latest price of a stock before deciding to buy or sell. This approach ensures that financial statements reflect real-time value, providing a clearer picture of overall financial health.
net interest marginfinancial
Net interest margin measures how much a bank earns from lending and investing compared with what it pays for funding, expressed as a percentage of its interest-earning assets. Think of it like a grocery store’s markup: it shows the gap between buying cost and selling price per dollar of goods — here, the cost is interest paid and the sale is interest received. Investors watch it because a higher margin usually means a bank is more profitable and better at managing interest rate and credit conditions.
sofrfinancial
The Secured Overnight Financing Rate (SOFR) is a market benchmark that measures the cost of borrowing cash overnight using U.S. Treasury securities as collateral. Investors watch SOFR because it acts like a speedometer for short-term interest costs—affecting loan rates, bond yields and the pricing of interest-rate contracts—so movements change borrowing expenses, cash returns and the value of interest-sensitive investments.
allowance for credit lossesfinancial
Allowance for credit losses is a reserve set aside by a financial institution to cover potential losses from borrowers who may not repay their loans. It acts like a safety net, helping the institution prepare for loans that might turn sour. For investors, it signals how cautious the institution is about the quality of its loans and potential risks to its financial health.
initial public offeringfinancial
An initial public offering (IPO) is when a private company first sells its shares to the public and becomes a stock-listed company. It matters because it allows the company to raise money from a wide range of investors, helping it grow, while giving early shareholders a way to sell some of their ownership.
